title: Runtime: safer TP defaults (concurrency + batch guardrails) behind feature flag
author: Julian Moore
release_notes: Adds feature-flagged TP guardrails that cap prefill/decode concurrency and batch sizing to reduce likelihood of TP stalls during rollout of deeper scheduler/NCCL fixes. No behavior change unless enabled via runtime.tp.guardrails.v1 or per-cluster overrides.
body:
Title: Runtime: safer TP defaults (concurrency + batch guardrails) behind feature flag

Context
We have repeated reports of TP replicas hanging under sustained mixed prefill/decode + bursty concurrency (see SUP-48321, SUP-48344; also linked to ongoing ENG-4821/ENG-4824 work). While root-cause fixes are landing (scheduler ordering, NCCL stream sync, watchdog), we still need a low-risk operational mitigation we can roll out quickly to Dedicated canaries.

This PR introduces a feature-flagged guardrail set for TP replicas that reduces the probability of starvation / collective mismatch scenarios by:
- capping concurrent decode microbatches per TP replica
- limiting prefill batch tokens under mixed workloads
- bounding prefill queue depth / admission to avoid long prefill bursts starving decode + collectives

The intent is NOT to "solve" TP hangs, but to reduce incidence while deeper fixes roll through canary and to provide an easy on/off lever for SRE during incidents.

What changed
- New feature flag: runtime.tp.guardrails.v1
  - default: OFF globally
  - intended rollout: Dedicated canary clusters first (release plan tracked in ENG-4829)
- When enabled for TP replicas, apply guardrail defaults unless explicitly overridden by cluster config:
  - max_decode_concurrency_per_replica: 2 (was effectively unbounded aside from global worker limits)
  - max_inflight_prefills_per_replica: 1 (new; prevents prefill pileups)
  - max_prefill_batch_tokens: 16384 (new; tuned for A100/H100 mixed prompt distributions)
  - prefill_queue_soft_limit: 8 (new; admission control backpressure)
  - prefer_decode_on_mixed_load: true (new; small bias to keep decode iterations progressing)
- Adds structured log event at replica init: tp_guardrails_applied=true/false + the resolved values (so we can correlate outcomes in incident review).
- Adds metrics:
  - runtime_tp_guardrails_enabled{cluster,replica}
  - runtime_tp_admission_rejections_total{reason}
- Updates docs in code comments + config schema with "do not enable for non-TP replicas" guidance.

Why these numbers
These values came out of repro runs from benchmark-lab mixed-workload harness (see ENG-4822 / benchmark-lab PR-97) and align with what oncall has been doing manually during incidents (reduce concurrency; constrain batch sizes). The goal is to keep TP replicas from entering long prefill-only regimes where decode collectives get delayed long enough to trigger downstream timeouts and eventually a stall.

Risk / performance impact
- Expected: throughput reduction on prefill-heavy workloads when flag enabled (admission control). This is considered acceptable for the canary window because the failure mode we’re trading off against is replica wedging + autoscaling thrash.
- Decode latency should improve at p95/p99 under bursty concurrency due to reduced queueing.
- Flag is OFF by default; enabling is per-environment/per-cluster.

Rollout plan (high level)
1) Land behind flag.
2) Enable in one Dedicated canary cluster for affected account(s) during a low-risk window with SRE support.
3) Watch: request timeout rate, TP heartbeat gaps, admission rejection rate, and customer-perceived streaming stability.
4) If stable, expand to additional Dedicated clusters as part of runtime 1.19 canary (ENG-4829).

Testing
- Unit tests for config resolution precedence (global defaults < guardrails defaults < cluster overrides < per-model overrides)
- Integration test in runtime config loader for "flag on only for TP" behavior
- Manual validation in staging: enabling flag yields expected structured log + metrics

Changelog / commits
- 0d4c3c2 runtime/config: add runtime.tp.guardrails.v1 feature flag + schema
- 4a9bf11 runtime/scheduler: apply tp guardrail defaults to admission control
- 7c1ae88 runtime/metrics: add guardrails enabled + rejection counters
- 19d0a6d tests: config precedence coverage + TP-only guardrail test
- bbe12c9 docs: inline config docs + oncall notes (internal)

Files / areas touched (high level)
- runtime/config/schema.yaml
- runtime/config/loader.cc
- runtime/scheduler/admission_control.cc
- runtime/scheduler/replica_limits.h
- runtime/observability/metrics_runtime_tp.cc
- runtime/logging/structured_events.cc
- runtime/tests/config_resolution_test.cc

Reviewer notes
- This PR intentionally keeps guardrails minimal and reversible. We should avoid embedding long-term policy here; once ENG-4824/ENG-4826 land broadly, we can revisit whether any of these should become defaults (or be removed).

---
Conversation (selected)

Sofia Ivanova (review): I like the direction. Two concerns: (1) make sure prefill_queue_soft_limit doesn’t affect non-TP replicas; (2) please document precedence when both per-model and per-cluster overrides exist.

Julian Moore (author): Good call. I’ve gated the entire block on tp_world_size > 1 and added a precedence test + comment in loader.cc.

Rafael Mendes (review): From SRE perspective, can we get a metric that tells us the flag is actually active on the replica? Also, can we include a log line with resolved values so oncall doesn’t have to grep config dumps.

Julian Moore (author): Added runtime_tp_guardrails_enabled gauge and a structured init event with resolved caps.

Noah Patel (review): The max_prefill_batch_tokens default might be too aggressive for long-context customers. Can we (a) make it explicit that this is a canary mitigation and (b) allow an override without disabling the rest of the guardrails?

Julian Moore (author): Yes—each cap is overrideable independently. The guardrails defaults only apply when the value is unset. Added config docs and an example.

Aisha Bello (review): Please include label(s) or tag(s) in metrics to break down rejections by reason so we can alert on pathological rejection loops.

Julian Moore (author): Added reason label (queue_full, prefill_tokens_cap, decode_concurrency_cap).

Connor O'Brien (release): Once merged, I’ll wire this into the runtime 1.19 canary checklist and ensure we have a rollback step (disable flag) in the runbook.

Merge
Merged via squash on 2025-03-03.

Follow-ups
- Coordinate enablement window + cluster list with SRE (ENG-4829)
- Validate impact in perf-canary TP stress scenarios (ENG-4828)
- If rejection rate is high, consider dynamic caps keyed off observed queueing/heartbeat (out of scope here)
